items.summary: Similar to Bajaj Auto and its partners, Hero and Harley duo have just made the transition from 440cc to 350cc and launch will happen soon

In China, Harley-Davidson has partnered with QJ Motor to offer X350 and it should not be confused with the soon-to-launch X350T in India from Hero and Harley duo. The Chinese offering is a liquid-cooled parallel-twin motorcycle, in comparison and costs CNY 33,388 (around Rs 4.77 lakh). Harley Davidson X350T for India has been spied undisguised ahead of launch. items.title: Top 50 Motorcycles H1 FY2027 – Splendor, Shine, Pulsar, Apache, Classic 350

India’s domestic motorcycle sales reached 69,28,700 units in the first half of FY2027, up 10.44% from 62,73,944 units in April–September 2025. The segment added 6,54,756 units year-on-year and remained the largest contributor to domestic two-wheeler volumes. Hero Splendor registered 21,30,637 units, growing 19.69% over 17,80,081 units a year earlier. Its increase of 3,50,556 units was the largest absolute gain among the ranked motorcycle families. Splendor alone accounted for 30.75% of domestic motorcycle sales. Honda Shine 125/SP125 followed with 9,65,571 units, up 11.09% from 8,69,190 units. Together, the top two entries contributed 44.69% of motorcycle volumes. Bajaj Pulsar retained third position despite a 6.86% decline. Sales stood at 6,33,015 units, down from 6,79,612 units. KTM has introduced ride-by-wire throttle control, a bi-directional quickshifter, traction control and two ride modes as standard equipment on the 200 Duke. The quickshifter enables clutchless upshifts and downshifts, while Street and Rain modes allow riders to adapt power delivery to the conditions. Traction control helps manage rear-wheel traction. These functions can be accessed through the updated TFT instrument interface, which allows riders to manage the traction control, ride modes and quickshifter settings. The additions bring features associated with KTM’s larger motorcycles to its 200cc streetfighter. Another feature confirmed in the official announcement is Crawl Assist. items.title: 2027 Kawasaki Z900 launched at Rs 9.99 lakh
items.summary: Kawasaki has launched the 2027 model year Z900 super-naked in India with two new colours as the only change. Tap to know more.
items.text: The Z900 got a comprehensive makeover for model year 2025, and Kawasaki has managed to keep the price at a rather sweet Rs 9.99 lakh despite the GST revision. For 2027, the brand is changing only the colour options offered and has left the motorcycle untouched, including the aforementioned ex-showroom price. To recap, Kawasaki refreshed the entire design of the Z900 in 2025 , giving it a sharper Sugomi styling and an enhanced suite of electronics. Some of these include a completely new 5-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity, turn-by-turn navigation, cornering-sensitive ABS and traction control, and cruise control. All of that gets carried over to 2027, as does the 948cc inline-four liquid-cooled engine making 124hp at 9,500rpm and 98.6Nm at 7,700rpm. Other cycle parts remain unchanged as well, including the USD fork and backlink monoshock units, as well as front and rear brakes. The full electronics suite and the rebound- and spring-adjustable suspension at both ends have been carried over too. New for 2027 are the two colour options, white with a green frame and grey with a black frame. The model year 2026’s candy lime green with a grey frame and black with a gold frame options have been discontinued. Deliveries are expected to commence today. 2026 Kawasaki Z900 launched at Rs 9.99 lakh 2025 Kawasaki Z900 launched at Rs 9.52 lakh

items.text: Recently, we reported that an updated version of the KTM 200 Duke, the Austro-Indian brand’s first motorcycle in the country, was expected soon with multiple new features. Now, the brand has launched it at Rs 2.07 lakh with upgrades that bring it closer to its bigger brother, the 390 Duke. The 200 Duke has essentially remained the same since its second generation was launched in 2020, receiving minor changes since then by way of a TFT display, an updated left switch cube, a new colour, a larger 320mm front disc brake and lighter alloy wheels, the last two straight from its bigger brother, the 390 Duke . KTM clearly wasn’t done for the year, as it has now given the bike a bunch more features. Its expensive price leaves the 200 Duke competing with 200s as well as 250s from other brands, and these upgrades should help soften that blow. The new upgrades are traction control, ride-by-wire, two ride modes (Street and Rain), a bi-directional quickshifter and last but not least, an up-to-date switch cube for the right side as well. Besides these changes, the motorcycle retains its second-generation styling and other mechanical parts. It has the 199.5cc single-cylinder liquid-cooled engine that makes 25hp at 10,000rpm and 19.3Nm at 8,000rpm, WP Apex-made 43mm USD fork and monoshock suspension units, a tubular trellis frame and, of course, the tyres and wheels, all of which remain unchanged. items.summary: SHAD is expanding its Terra adventure range into motorcycle protection with upper and lower crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS. Possible India availability after EICMA 2026.
items.text: SHAD Terra crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS are set to make their show debut at EICMA 2026. This is an important expansion of the Spanish accessory maker’s adventure-focused Terra range. Until now Terra has largely been associated with panniers, top boxes and soft luggage. The addition of motorcycle protection takes the range into a new category and SHAD has chosen one of the most established large adventure motorcycles as its first application. There’s two separate protection systems for the BMW R 1300 GS. Upper Crash Bars are designed to protect the fuel tank, radiator and upper bodywork. The Lower Crash Bars concentrate on the engine, crankcase or oil sump area and exhaust headers. This modular arrangement is useful because owners can choose the degree of protection they need. Although the upper bars require the corresponding lower crash bars to be installed first. Both assemblies are made from AISI 304 stainless steel. SHAD uses 25mm-diameter tubing with a 2mm wall thickness, with the structure designed to provide high strength without adding unnecessary width around the motorcycle. The bars mount directly to the R 1300 GS ’ existing chassis mounting points, meaning installation does not require cutting or drilling the motorcycle. You can pick between two finishes. items.title: Moto Guzzi Trip 500 unveiled in Europe
items.summary: The Trip 500 is Moto Guzzi's smallest-capacity offering and would be a great option for Indian buyers if launched here.
items.text: Moto Guzzi, part of the Piaggio Group, has unveiled its new Trip 500 roadster in Europe. The Trip 500 will become Moto Guzzi's small-capacity offering when it goes on sale in early 2027, with Moto Guzzi looking to tap into the entry-level roadster market. The Trip 500 comes with a 500cc, liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine, making a claimed 48bhp. With Moto Guzzi falling under the Piaggio Group, it's possible that '500cc' might be a marketing term, and the engine is closely related to Aprilia's 457cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin, evidenced by similar engine cases and the underbelly exhaust. The Trip 500 could come with a different state of tune or gearing to suit the roadster's character. The Trip 500 also uses a USD fork setup and a large front disc with radially-mounted ByBre braking hardware. The Mandello del Lario-based automaker calls the Trip 500 the 'first of a new generation' for Moto Guzzi, bucking the Italian manufacturer's trend of using transversely mounted, air-cooled V-twin engines. The Trip 500's performance targets the A2 license class in Europe, which has a performance cap of 48bhp, and a power-to-weight limit for larger-capacity models. Moto Guzzi hopes the Trip 500 will appeal to newer riders or those returning to motorcycling, and draw them to the Moto Guzzi brand. items.title: Flying Flea C6 Expands to Pune With 10 Centres
items.summary: Royal Enfield’s electric brand has entered its third Indian city with a wide sales and service footprint.
items.text: Flying Flea C6 has expanded to Pune at a price of Rs 2.79 lakh ex-showroom making the city the third Indian market for Royal Enfield’s electric motorcycle brand after Bengaluru and Hyderabad. And at what scale, Flying Flea opened 10 sales and service centres across Pune from the outset. The network covers Pimple Saudagar, Wakad, Market Yard, Wakdewadi, Chinchwad, Kondhwa, Yerawada, Wagholi, Baner and Kasarwadi areas. Dealers include Nomadic Motorbikes, Kings Royal Riders, Dhone Automobiles, Brahma Motors, Hridaan Motors, Legacy Automotive, Chopada Motors and Vogue Motocorp LLP. The expansion follows the C6’s rollout in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Flying Flea currently operates 12 sales and service centres in Bengaluru and another four in Hyderabad. With Pune adding 10 more, the company now has 26 touchpoints across its first three Indian cities. Royal Enfield says each Pune dealer is equipped to provide both routine maintenance and dedicated technical support. Pune city has a sizeable two-wheeler population, a strong technology and automotive industry presence and a large base of riders already familiar with premium motorcycles. It also has a mix of dense urban commuting and peripheral roads that fits Flying Flea’s city-focused positioning.

items.title: Updated KTM 200 Duke Launched in India at Rs. 2.07 Lakh
items.summary: The updated KTM 200 Duke has been launched in India at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom). The motorcycle has received some new features, including a traction control system, a bi-directional quick shifter, among others. Here’s a detailed breakdown:
items.text: KTM has updated the 200 Duke in India, and the bike has received some substantial updates. The updated bike is now priced at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom); this makes it Rs. 1,552 more expensive. It now comes with a new ride-by-wire throttle, unlocking some new features alongside tweaks to its underpinnings. On the features front, the bike now gets two riding modes: Street and Rain, likely to alter the throttle response. In addition, the brand has added a traction control system for better safety. An interesting bit taken from the higher-capacity 390 Duke is the crawl feature. This is a low-speed assist that prevents the bike from stalling at lower speeds, and should make city rides a lot easier. Lastly, for spirited riding, the Duke now gets a bidirectional quickshifter for clutchless up- and downshifts. The underpinnings have been revised, with the bike now getting a 43mm inverted fork and a fatter 150-section rear tyre. This is a welcome change, as the brand had updated the bike earlier with a smaller 37mm WP Apex fork and a thinner 140-section tyre, which felt like a slight downgrade . Apart from the features and underpinning changes, the bike now comes with two additional colours: Liquid-carbon and a full black shade. Aside from these, the bike remains mechanically unchanged. It continues to be powered by the same 199.5cc, single-cylinder, liquid-cooled motor producing 24.67bhp and 19.3Nm.

items.title: 2027 Kawasaki Z900 at Rs 9.99 Lakh Barely Changes
items.summary: 2027 Z900 gets two fresh colour schemes and a slightly revised India-spec power figure. Everything else from the electronics, chassis, suspension and braking remain the same.
items.text: Kawasaki India has updated the Z900 for 2027 model year at Rs 9.99 lakh ex-showroom. Now unlike the substantial overhaul that arrived with the previous update, this new MY27 motorcycle is largely a colour and homologation refresh. 2027 Z900 is now available in Ebony with Metallic Carbon Gray and Metallic Spark Black, and the awesome Pearl Blizzard White with Plasma Lime Green. Both these colourways are new to the India-spec motorcycle. The outgoing 2026 Z900 was offered in Metallic Matte Graphenesteel Gray with Metallic Flat Spark Black and Candy Lime Green with Metallic Carbon Gray. Both of which have now disappeared from Kawasaki India’s 2027 listing. There is, however, one small difference in the India-spec engine figures. The new Z900 continues with the 948cc liquid-cooled inline-four, but Kawasaki India now lists maximum output at 121bhp. For comparison, the official 2026 India page listed the same engine at 122bhp with identical torque output. That means the figure has fallen by 1bhp for MY27. Kawasaki has not explained the reason for this change. It could be related to homologation or the way the output is being declared for the latest model year. There is another small numerical difference. Kawasaki India now lists the 2027 Z900 at 213kg kerb, one kilogram heavier than the 212kg figure for the 2026 model. Estimated dry weight hence rises from 192kg to 193kg.

items.text: Bajaj Pulsar N250 2V is nearing the end of its run in India with production of the existing motorcycle understood to have stopped. The outgoing model will continue to be available through dealerships until remaining inventory is exhausted after which the recently launched Pulsar N250SS will effectively take over the quarter-litre N-series position. Bajaj Auto has not yet issued an official discontinuation announcement for the older N250. The website continues to list the motorcycle at Rs 1,42,202, ex-showroom Delhi, with an active booking option. Customers may still find the older motorcycle at dealerships for some time depending on local inventory. The bigger clue comes from Bajaj’s own description of the newly launched Pulsar N250SS. The company calls it an “upgraded version of the Pulsar N250 ”, rather than positioning it as a separate derivative intended to sit permanently alongside the existing bike. The mechanical changes also make the replacement strategy fairly obvious. The outgoing Pulsar N250 uses a 249.07cc, single-cylinder, oil-cooled SOHC engine with two valves. It produces 24bhp and 21.5Nm and is paired with a five-speed gearbox. Pulsar N250SS takes that same basic quarter-litre idea considerably further. Its engine moves to a four-valve head and produces 24.5bhp and 22Nm. More importantly, Bajaj has replaced the five-speed transmission with a six-speed gearbox addressing one of the clearest limitations of the outgoing motorcycle.

items.text: Rejoice, avid Classic 350 owners and fans! Royal Enfield seems to be preparing a version of its popular retro cruiser with what appears to be cross-spoked rims. The demo unit on display at a dealership was seen with black powder-coated cross-spoke rims and CEAT tubeless tyres. Classic 350 has been offered with tube tyres on its spoked wheel variants for as long as the model has been on sale, while tubeless tyres have only been available with variants that feature alloy wheels. This meant that historically, buyers would have to choose between the convenience of, and lower maintenance with, tubeless tyres, or the style and charm of old-school spokes and tubes. Tubeless tyres offer several advantages over tube-type tyres. Tubeless tyres hold air pressure within the tyre itself, which seals against the tyre's bead. This means punctures encountered with tubeless tyres are safer, since the tyre loses pressure more gradually, rather than all at once. Moreover, these punctures are easier to patch since there is no inner tube, so neither the wheel nor the tyre has to be removed from the motorcycle. It remains to be seen whether Royal Enfield will release this in a standalone variant, or whether RE plans to retire tubed tyres from their range entirely. Regardless of how the automaker plans to roll it out, these cross-spoke wheels should be available for purchase as an add-on accessory that existing owners can also benefit from. The pass will be valid only at the particular toll plaza for which it has been issued. It will not provide toll-free access across other toll plazas on national highways. The Central Government may revise the prescribed fees annually on April 1. Motorists considering the pass should therefore check the applicable fee and eligibility requirements before applying. The network operates under dealer partnerships with Nomadic Motorbikes, Kings Royal Riders, Dhone Automobiles, Brahma Motors, Hridaan Motors, Legacy Automotive, Chopada Motors, and Vogue Motocorp LLP. items.text: Hero MotoCorp expects industry growth to moderate to mid-to-high single digits in H2 FY27 following strong double-digit growth in the first half. Hero MotoCorp expects India's two-wheeler industry growth to moderate to mid-to-high single digits during the second half of FY27, following strong double-digit growth in the first six months. Speaking during the company's Q2 FY27 earnings call on Thursday, Chief Executive Officer Harshavardhan Chitale said the higher base created by strong sales following last year's GST changes would moderate growth, although underlying demand remained healthy. "As we see today and are planning for H2, we are looking at still mid-to-high single-digit growth. Even ICE will be in growth with low single digits. And EV will then take it to a high single digit for the industry," Chitale said. The outlook follows a strong first half for India's two-wheeler industry. According to VAHAN registrations, industry retail sales increased by more than 27% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, with internal combustion engine (ICE) two-wheelers growing 23% and electric models registering 82% growth. For the first half, industry retail sales increased by more than 20%. The pygmy hog was believed to be extinct by the mid-20th century. In Assam, the Pygmy Hog Conservation Programme was launched in 1995. A year later, six pygmy hogs were taken out of Assam’s grasslands to Manas National Park. Conservationists feared that their dwindling numbers could lead to extinction if they were not bred in captivity. The pygmy hog depends significantly on dense grasslands to feed. However, with the burning of grasslands and their conversion into tea estates brought down their numbers. Since 1996, there has been a 32-fold increase in the numbers of pygmy hogs. Since 2020, six groups of pygmy hogs have been released into the Manas National Park. Earlier this year, the Standing Committee on National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL) included the pygmy hog in the list of critically endangered species so that it receives focused conservation support under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (CSS-IDWH). The scheme provides financial assistance to states to protect species under a wildlife recovery programme. events.title: Motul On India’s Biking Boom And The Future Of Riding
events.summary: Motul India’s Milind Acharya on the country’s booming biking culture, rising premium motorcycle segment and the future of performance riding.
events.text: Q1. What’s fuelling India’s fast-growing biking culture right now? A few forces are converging at once. Rising disposable incomes and easier access to finance have put mid-capacity and premium motorcycles within reach of a much younger buyer than we saw a decade ago. At the same time, riding has shifted from being purely a commute or a college obsession to a lifestyle statement — weekend rides, long-distance touring, and motorsport fandom are now aspirational in a way they weren’t before. Almost every city has multiple riding clubs who happen to find a reason to meet over the weekend. Infrastructure has helped too — better highways and mountain roads have opened up touring circuits that simply weren’t practical earlier. And social media has turned individual riders into micro-communities; a single Instagram reel of a Spiti or Leh-Ladakh run can pull hundreds of new riders into the culture. We’re also seeing a genuine rise in women riders and first-time premium buyers, which is broadening the base rather than just deepening it among existing enthusiasts. To put a number on it, we will end up engaging with 30,000-plus riders this year through the biking communities we work with — showcasing new launches and recommending the right products for their motorcycles. lead.headline: Ultraviolette adds cruise control, Park Assist and a battery pyro fuse to the X-47 Venom
lead.text: Ultraviolette has announced three additions to the X-47 Venom electric motorcycle on its own YouTube channel. Cruise control now holds a set speed. Park Assist uses the integrated dual dashcam, with front and rear cameras and a 120 degree wide angle, to help when moving in reverse. And a Pyro Fuse, a battery safety device taken from four-wheelers, isolates the battery instantly during critical events.
lead.why: The X-47 Venom is the most searched bike in India this week, and cruise control is still rare on Indian electric motorcycles.
